lens: human connection, trust, agency, communication, collaboration

findings.observation: Audio capture has a clear purpose field, an explicit recruiter authorization toggle, foreground-only recording, local-only storage, and deletion, but the durable local receipt preserves only the purpose and file facts. It does not preserve who authorized the recording, when authorization was obtained, its scope, or a revocation reference. The gate is therefore an honest human attestation, not durable consent provenance.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-FINAL-20260824-01; ios-audio-idle.png sha256 9ff3df29fc21e449caa3788fd8f1679406b832109b0fdfcead7cfb4754860c19; AudioSignalCaptureView.swift:78-110 requires permission, purpose, and the authorization toggle; AudioSignalCaptureStore.swift:32-41 blocks start without the toggle and purpose; AudioSignalCapture.swift:9-18 defines the persisted receipt without authorization provenance; p0-journey-runtime.json P0-09 passed local authorization, payload, and deletion with zero external effects.
findings.user_impact: A candidate is protected from hidden background capture and cloud processing, but a mistaken or dishonest recruiter attestation could still create a sensitive local recording with no durable record of the candidate's permission. That weakens later trust repair, audit, or revocation handling even though V1 never uploads the audio.
findings.recommendation: Keep the current no-upload boundary and add the smallest structured local authorization record: authorization basis, authorizing party, recorded-at time, permitted purpose, and optional expiry or revocation reference. Show that record beside the saved receipt and make revocation lead directly to verified deletion.
findings.verification: Attempt to start audio without each required authorization field and verify no microphone session begins; complete an authorized recording and verify the local receipt reads back the exact authorization scope; revoke it and verify audio plus authorization metadata are deleted and no downstream Proposal or external effect exists.

findings.observation: Canonical Actions require a workspace owner and Today selects only the current user's open Actions, but the visible due-action reason and Pursuit detail show status and due date without naming the accountable human. Proposals and evidence-backed gaps likewise do not expose a review owner or missed-commitment recovery path on the attention surface.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-FINAL-20260824-01; requirement-trace.json V1-CRM-004 is proven for owner, status, and due date; PursuitWorkspace.swift:46-65 filters Actions by currentUserID but formats due Actions as Due <date> · internal action only; RelationshipArchiveView.swift:853-880 displays action title, status, due date, and external-effect boundary but not owner; ios-canonical-today.png sha256 1cae803e0798090072864a2a1682d1faa3e62208f0fd8813b0dd4219d89ca681 shows Proposal reasons without a named review owner or response commitment.
findings.user_impact: The system prevents an automated candidate nudge, yet a shared recruiting team can still lose sight of which human owes the next internal response. If that ownership fails, the candidate may experience avoidable waiting even though the underlying schema is correct.
findings.recommendation: Show the accountable human, commitment time, and current handoff state on every due Action and review-worthy dependency. When a commitment is missed, route attention to the internal owner or escalation path and keep any candidate update visibly human-owned rather than generating another candidate chase.
findings.verification: Create a synthetic client or hiring-manager dependency with an assigned owner and overdue commitment; verify Today and Pursuit detail name that human, show the missed commitment, offer an internal recovery path, and create neither a candidate nudge nor any external effect.

findings.observation: The final build correctly derives the Today date and retains source timezone in canonical evidence, but the Proposal review renders the observed time as a raw UTC timestamp and omits sourceTimezone. Today shows evidence count and revision rather than evidence age. Relative candidate language such as next Tuesday is therefore reviewable but not yet easy to interpret safely across timezones.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-FINAL-20260824-01; ios-canonical-today.png shows Monday, 24 August and revision-backed attention; ios-canonical-proposal-review.png sha256 4a126b907a237de4623878f2ef368d011dc1594bb56dacc333ea07bea3239040 shows The final conversation works next Tuesday and Observed: 2026-08-23T21:14:51.357Z; PursuitProposalReviewClient.swift:259-295 decodes sourceTimezone; RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:32-48 displays observedAt but omits sourceTimezone; PursuitProposalReviewStore.swift:100-121 blocks unavailable, deleted, unreviewed, or attribution-unconfirmed evidence.
findings.user_impact: The product will not contact anyone automatically, but a recruiter can still misread when a candidate meant next Tuesday or how fresh the evidence is, leading to a poorly timed human follow-up later. Correct data without human-readable timing is only partial protection of the candidate's attention.
findings.recommendation: Display evidence age plus an absolute time in both source and recruiter timezones. Preserve relative date phrases as explicit ambiguity and require a human clarification or resolved timezone before they can become a due date or scheduling Action.
findings.verification: Review a synthetic next Tuesday message authored in Asia/Shanghai while the device uses a different timezone; verify both time contexts and evidence age are visible, no due date is inferred, and a scheduling Action remains unresolved until a human supplies the exact date and timezone.

strengths: The connected review shows exact candidate words, person, contextual role, attributed speaker, source, channel, observed time, attribution status, and review status before presenting an explicitly labeled inference and its effect (RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:22-180; frozen Proposal screenshot).

Every Proposal item supports Confirm, Edit, Reject, or Unresolved; edited values are validated, deleted or unreviewed evidence blocks apply, stale revision conflicts do not overwrite, response loss locks the operation, and success appears only after canonical revisioned readback with empty external effects (PursuitProposalReviewClient.swift:31-47; PursuitProposalReviewStore.swift:83-121 and 176-274; pursuit-proposal-runtime.json verdict pass).

Today derives the actual date, ranks governed work rather than people, limits owned Actions to the current user, keeps no-action visible, labels synthetic preview state, and refuses to substitute cached or fixture candidate facts when the canonical workspace cannot be read (PursuitWorkspace.swift:22-105; RelationshipArchiveView.swift:366-478 and 642-759).

Capture stays intentional: typed words can remain protected and local, attribution begins without a forced answer, unresolved attribution cannot support the optional Proposal, and audio cannot appear as recording until authorization, foreground state, microphone permission, and recorder success are all true (frozen Text Signal and Audio screenshots; ios-full-suite-runtime.json and ios-system-capture-runtime.json).

The frozen runtime passed 12/12 P0 journeys and 51 assertions with zero external effects; the iOS full suite recorded 89 passed, 0 failed, and one explicitly allowed legacy skip; small-device dark AX5 capture and review checks passed.
missing_evidence: No candidate-facing artifact, candidate-visible message, candidate correction interaction, delivery or closure receipt, or authorized candidate feedback study exists in the frozen bundle. This does not block the internal no-send V1, but it prevents a claim about the candidate's experienced communication quality.
No design-partner field comparison shows that recruiters actually follow through faster, reduce unnecessary candidate interruption, or use internal owner and due fields consistently.
No synthetic end-to-end journey covers a missed recruiter, client, or hiring-manager commitment followed by a humane candidate update or closure; external sending is explicitly out of V1 scope.

Production authentication, retention and deletion operations, regional data controls, provider reconciliation, cross-tenant adversarial testing, and any real candidate data remain intentionally unavailable.
Manual VoiceOver completion of the full critical journey and physical-device Action Button, microphone, and interruption behavior remain unobserved.
Five credentialed live Claude Agent SDK trials are missing; deterministic same-protocol safety is proven, but live-provider release behavior is not.
open_questions: What minimum authorization basis should be stored locally so a recruiter can prove the scope of an audio recording without retaining unnecessary candidate data?
When a client or hiring manager owns the blocker, how will that human and the candidate-update commitment appear on Today without turning the candidate into another task metric?

What authorized candidate-side study will test whether the eventual human communication is clear, well-timed, easy to correct, and respectful without introducing real candidate content into this frozen panel?
